source_text: Ὃς ἂν οὑν ἐλθὼν διδάξῃ ὑμᾶς ταῦτα πάντα τὰ προειρημένα, δέξασθε αὐτόν: ἐὰν δὲ αὐτὸς ὁ διδάσκων στραφεὶς διδάσκῃ ἄλλην διδαχὴν εἰς τὸ καταλῦσαι, μὴ αὐτοῦ ἀκούσητε: εἰς δὲ τὸ προσθεῖναι δικαιοσύνην καὶ γνῶσιν κυρίου, δέξασθε αὐτὸν ὡς κύριον. Περὶ δὲ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ προφητῶν, κατὰ τὸ δόγμα τοῦ εὐαγγελίου οὕτω ποιήσατε. πᾶς δὲ ἀπόστολος ἐρχόμενος πρὸς ὑμᾶς δεχθήτω ὡς κύριος: οὐ μενεῖ δὲ εἰ μὴ ἡμέραν μίαν: ἐὰν δὲ ᾖ χρεία, καὶ τὴν ἄλλην: τρεῖς δὲ ἐὰν μείνῃ, ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν. ἐξερχόμενος δὲ ὁ ἀπόστολος μηδὲν λαμβανέτω εἰ μὴ ἄρτον, ἕως οὖ αὐλισθῇ: ἐὰν δὲ ἀργύριον αἰτῇ, ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστί. Καὶ πάντα προφήτην λαλοῦντα ἐν πνεύματι οὐ πειράσετε οὐδὲ διακρινεῖτε: πᾶσα γὰρ ἁμαρτία ἀφεθήσεται, αὕτη δὲ ἡ ἁμαρτία οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται. οὐ πᾶς δὲ ὁ λαλῶν ἐν πνεύματι προφήτης ἐστίν, ἀλλ’ ἐὰν ἔχῃ τοὺς τρόπους κυρίου. ἀπὸ οὖν τῶν τρόπων γνωσθήσεται ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης καὶ ὁ προφήτης. καὶ πᾶς προφήτης ὁρίζων τράπεζαν ἐν πνεύματι οὐ φάγεται ἀπ’ αὐτῆς, εἰ δὲ μήγε ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστί. πᾶς δὲ προφήτης διδάσκων τὴν ἀλήθειαν, εἰ ἃ διδάσκει οὐ ποιεῖ. ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστί. πᾶς δὲ προφήτης δεδοκιμασμένος, ἀληθινός, ποιῶν εἰς μυστήριον κοσμικὸν ἐκκλησίας, μὴ διδάσκων δὲ ποιεῖν, ὅσα αὐτὸς ποιεῖ, οὐ κριθήσεται ἐφ̓ ὑμῶν: μετὰ θεοῦ γὰρ ἔχει τὴν κρίσιν: ὡσαύτως γὰρ ἐποίησαν καὶ οἱ ἀρχαῖοι προφῆται. ὃς δ’ ἂν εἴπῃ ἐν πνεύματι: δός μοι ἀργύρια ἢ ἕτερά τινα, οὐκ ἀκούσεσθε αὐτοῦ: ἐὰν δὲ περὶ ἄλλων ὑστερούντων εἴπῃ δοῦναι, μηδεὶς αὐτὸν κρινέτω.
pass_a_gloss: Whoever comes and teaches you all these things previously mentioned, receive him; but if he himself, the teacher, turns and teaches another teaching to destroy, do not listen to him; but to add righteousness and knowledge of the Lord, receive him as the Lord. Now concerning the apostles and prophets, do thus according to the doctrine of the gospel. And every apostle coming to you, let him be received as the Lord; he will not stay except one day; but if there is need, also the next; but if he stays three days, he is a false prophet. And the apostle going out, let him take nothing except bread, until he lodges; but if he asks for money, he is a false prophet. And every prophet speaking in the Spirit, do not test nor discern; for every sin will be forgiven, but this sin will not be forgiven. Not everyone speaking in the Spirit is a prophet, but if he has the ways of the Lord. Therefore, the false prophet and the prophet will be known from the ways. And every prophet who ordains a table in the Spirit, will not eat from it, but if he does, he is a false prophet. Every prophet teaching the truth, if he does not do what he teaches, is a false prophet. Every approved prophet, true, doing for the mystery of the church's worldly needs, but not teaching to do what he himself does, will not be judged by you; for he has judgment with God; for the ancient prophets did likewise. But whoever says in the Spirit: give me money or something else, do not listen to him; but if he says to give to others who are in need, let no one judge him.

choices.why: comparing the apostle's reception to the Lord's
referring to the community of believers

pass_b_english: Welcome anyone who comes and teaches you everything I have said before. But if that teacher turns around and teaches something different in order to undermine it, do not listen to him. On the other hand, if he teaches in order to add righteousness and knowledge of the Lord, welcome him as you would the Lord. Now concerning the apostles and prophets, follow these instructions in line with the teaching of the gospel. Every apostle who comes to you should be welcomed as the Lord. He should stay no more than one day; if necessary, he may stay a second. But if he stays three days, he is a false prophet. When an apostle leaves, he must take nothing but bread until he finds lodging. If he asks for money, he is a false prophet. Do not test or evaluate any prophet who speaks in the Spirit, for every other sin will be forgiven, but this sin will not be forgiven. Not everyone who speaks in the Spirit is a prophet—only one who lives in the Lord's ways. So the false prophet and the true prophet will be recognized by their conduct. Any prophet who sets a table in the Spirit must not eat from it; if he does, he is a false prophet. Any prophet who teaches the truth but does not practice what he teaches is a false prophet. But a proven, genuine prophet who acts for the mystery of the church's worldly needs without teaching others to do as he does—do not judge him, for his judgment rests with God, just as the ancient prophets did. If anyone says in the Spirit, "Give me money or anything else," do not listen to him. But if he urges you to give to others in need, no one should judge him.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the distinction between the sin that is forgiven and the sin that is not, the criteria for identifying false prophets (staying three days, asking for money, eating from the table, or not practicing what is taught), and the specific instructions regarding apostles and prophets. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek source.
